To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) fs-LST can be used to generate surface functionalities for tribological purposes; (2) surface functionalities can be achieved with different laser processing strategies (i.e., laser ablation and laser-induced periodic surface structures); (3) surface functionalities can also be achieved on different substrate materials; (4) surface functionalities can improve the tribological performance, in terms of friction and wear; (5) the improvement of tribological performance is related to the surface topography and/or surface chemistry;
the tribological performance of fs-LST is strongly dependent on the surface topography and the lubrication conditions.
the laser-generated micro- and nanoscale surface topographies are able to reduce friction by 20% and wear by 40% under lubricated sliding conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of laser-textured surfaces with enhanced tribological properties.
the following questions: (i) What is the influence of fs-LST on the tribological properties of materials?

the following topics: (1) the influence of fs-LST on the tribological behavior of steel and titanium alloys, (2) the effect of laser-induced surface oxidation on tribological performance, and (3) the effect of additives on the tribological properties of laser-textured surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tribological performance of laser-textured surfaces strongly depends on the specific surface topographies, and on the material, lubricant, and tribological test conditions.
fs-LST can significantly reduce the friction and wear of steel and titanium alloys, but the tribological performance is strongly dependent on the surface topography and the type of lubricants used.
laser texturing can be a promising technology for improving the tribological behavior of surfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
laser-induced ripples and grooves are promising for tribological applications, while the tribological performance of laser-induced spikes is still under discussion.
the tribological performance of fs-LST is mainly determined by the surface topography and the material hardness.

the laser-irritation zone is the main parameter for the tribological performance, while the laser-irritation zone can be tailored by adjusting laser parameters (pulse energy, pulse duration, and repetition rate).
The main takeaway from our work is that
laser-generated surface structures with different morphologies can be used for friction and wear reduction in tribological contacts.
the friction coefficient of fs-LST surfaces is significantly lower than the corresponding untextured reference surfaces.
the friction and wear of laser-textured surfaces is highly sensitive to the specific tribological test conditions.
